Methods for nbreg objects

Source: R/methods-nbreg.R
nbreg-methods.Rd

Standard accessor, summary, and prediction methods for fits from nbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
predict(object, newdata, type = c("response", "link"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

object, x

An object of class "nbreg" (or "summary.nbreg" for the print method of a summary).

...

Further arguments (ignored or passed on to stats::printCoefmat()).

type

For residuals(): "response" (\(y_i - \hat\mu_i\)) or "pearson" (\((y_i-\hat\mu_i)/\sqrt{\hat\mu_i + \hat\mu_i^2/\hat\theta}\)). For predict(): "response" (\(\hat\mu\)) or "link" (\(\hat\eta = \log\hat\mu\)).

newdata

Optional data frame in which to look for covariates (and the offset variable) for prediction. If omitted, fitted values are used.

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

Value

coef(): estimated coefficients. vcov(): their covariance matrix. logLik(): a "logLik" object with df = number of coefficients + 1 (for \(\theta\)), so stats::AIC() and stats::BIC() work. fitted(): \(\hat\mu\). residuals(): see type. nobs(): number of observations. predict(): numeric vector. summary(): an object of class "summary.nbreg" with a coefficient table.

Examples

set.seed(2)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(200), g = factor(sample(c("a", "b"), 200, TRUE)))
d$y <- rnbinom(200, size = 2, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.4 * d$x + 0.3 * (d$g == "b")))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x + g, data = d)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x + g, data = d)
#> 
#> Pearson residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -1.1946 -0.7139 -0.2793  0.4788  3.6406 
#> 
#> Coefficients (NB2 with log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  0.58657    0.09615   6.101 1.06e-09 ***
#> x            0.28609    0.06268   4.564 5.01e-06 ***
#> gb           0.28533    0.13330   2.140   0.0323 *  
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Theta: 2.474  (SE 0.5774 )
#> Log-likelihood: -378.056 on 4 Df;  AIC: 764.112   BIC: 777.306 
#> Number of observations: 200   Outer iterations (IRLS + Newton): 4 
AIC(fit); BIC(fit)
#> [1] 764.1122
#> [1] 777.3055
head(residuals(fit, type = "pearson"))
#>          1          2          3          4          5          6 
#> -1.0288890 -1.0359851 -0.3374709 -0.2136776 -1.0963069  1.7307515 
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1), g = "b"))
#>        1        2        3 
#> 1.796449 2.391451 3.183522
